## What it is

LibreTranslate is machine translation that runs on the box: a web page and an HTTP API, with no cloud service behind it ([LibreTranslate/LibreTranslate](https://github.com/LibreTranslate/LibreTranslate)). The translation itself is done by Argos Translate language models. It is the Supply Depot's translation app (issue #129, NMD-04).

## Licences: the software and the models are separate

**Software:** `AGPL-3.0` (GitHub licence API). Market class **L2** (strong copyleft). OneMind runs upstream's unmodified image as a separate program and copies none of its code. AGPL adds one duty on top of the GPL: whoever *modifies* the program and lets people use it over a network must offer them the modified source. OneMind does not modify it, so pointing users to the upstream source is enough. There is no research licence-matrix row yet, so it is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10).

**Language models (content, not code):** the image is built without models; they are downloaded on first start from the Argos Translate package index ([argosopentech/argospm-index](https://github.com/argosopentech/argospm-index), commit `ff90de60728f`, read 2026-11-19). That index's README says the index is dual licensed MIT or CC0, but the index lists no licence per model. UNVERIFIED: the terms of each downloaded model package (they are trained on public parallel text whose own terms vary by corpus) were not checked. Until a model-by-model check is done, OneMind does not ship any model in an image or preinstall one; the person who installs the app downloads them.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment`, one container: `docker.io/libretranslate/libretranslate:v1.10.0`, pinned by digest (Docker Hub registry API, 2026-11-19; amd64 and arm64). The image runs as its own user `libretranslate` (UID/GID 1032, per `docker/Dockerfile` at v1.9.6, not re-read at v1.10.0) on port 5000.
- **Models on a volume:** Argos keeps models under `/home/libretranslate/.local`, so that path is the PVC `libretranslate-models` (5Gi). Then a restart or an update does not download them again. `fsGroup: 1032` makes the volume writable for the app user.
- **Only four languages by default** (`LT_LOAD_ONLY=en,es,fr,de`): every language adds a download and memory. Add language codes there to get more.
- **Internet once, then offline:** the first start needs internet to download the models; after that it runs offline. `LT_UPDATE_MODELS` stays at its default (off), so it never fetches again on its own.
- Two gunicorn workers (`LT_THREADS=2`); each loads the models, so memory grows with workers. Requests 100m CPU / 1Gi, limit 2 CPU / 3Gi (OneMind choices; upstream publishes none).
- The root filesystem stays writable, because the app writes its API-key and metrics databases under `/app/db`. Non-root, RuntimeDefault seccomp, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped, no service-account token.
- Probes: `GET /languages`; the startup probe allows 15 minutes for the first model download.

## First run

Source: [LibreTranslate docs](https://docs.libretranslate.com).

1. Install LibreTranslate from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-libretranslate`. The first start downloads the models (several minutes).
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:5000:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-libretranslate port-forward svc/libretranslate 5000:5000
   ```
3. Type text, pick the languages, read the translation. Programs use the same port: `POST /translate`.

## Not done yet

- Per-model licence check (UNVERIFIED above) and a licence-matrix row.
- No API keys or rate limits configured: anyone who can reach the port can use it. That is fine behind a port-forward; it needs keys before it is exposed on the LAN.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps.
- `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

**Pin bump (ma/market-bump-45-blocked-app-images, 2026-11-27, Refs #1232, Refs #234):** LibreTranslate v1.9.6 to v1.10.0. New optional settings (`--trust-forwarded-for`, `LT_TIMEOUT`) and glossaries; nothing required. The new pins were read from the registries with `crane`. They were **not** scanned: the Trivy vulnerability database could not be downloaded from the build sandbox, so this change claims no pass. The tier stays `blocked`; the CI gate decides.
